evidence.title: Launch a real loopback-only browser for the existing owner-authorized Command Incident to Investigate Case Timeline journey
evidence.goal: Replace test-only browser path with a runnable no-paid-API local first-party Go server mounting existing Command Work Queue and Investigate Case Timeline handlers, a minimal ephemeral browser Basic challenge, two independently checked synthetic owners and a visible corrected Case timeline. Real browser navigation; no network deployment, production identity provider or data source.
outputs: go run ./cmd/local-browser starts real 127.0.0.1 ephemeral HTTP server, displays one-time credentials and URL, supports actual browser Basic challenge
Following same-origin Incident Case link renders source-authorized Case Timeline HTML with supersession, filters and pages, no manually injected Authorization header
Negative live HTTP Basic principal/source denial and DNS rebinding Host tests
Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM cancellation closes the loopback HTTP server without unhandled exit.
acceptance_tests: A real loopback HTTP client authenticates as analyst and follows actual selected Incident-linked Case into owner-authorized Timeline HTML; source v1 is marked superseded by v2 and filters work
Commander with separate valid credentials can access Incident but not Investigate Case, even if URL is manually supplied; invalid/missing Basic secret denied
Host header spoof, unsupported/remote origin and unsupported path denied; no Basic credentials in links; no-store and no-referrer preserved
Go host+subcommand tests/vet/race and full mandatory engineering kernel pass on exact candidate SHA
Inject a failing entropy source, duplicate analyst/commander secrets, refused listen socket, and failed console writer; assert no running HTTP server and no credential leak.

rules: Strict tenant isolation and permission checking
